title: Comparison of Facial Feature Grading by an AI-Based System Versus Human Expert Grading on Images Under Standardized Clinical and At-Home Settings
authors: Danko, D.; Tlyachev, T.; Kiselev, K.; Bousseksou, L.; Camel, E.; Stamatas, G.; Georgievskaya, A.
abstract: Digital photography remains the gold standard for dermatological assessment, but reliance on standardized stationary image-capture systems limits trial scalability, whereas smartphones combined with computer vision artificial intelligence (AI) could enable hybrid and decentralized clinical trials (DCTs). This study assessed the facial feature grading of an AI-based system against expert panel consensus across three settings with decreasing acquisition control: Standard Studio Imaging (SSI), Clinic Smartphone Imaging (CSI), and Home Smartphone Imaging (HSI). Expert inter-rater reliability was good to excellent (median ICC 0.84-0.90), and the system showed high operator-independent test-retest repeatability across independently captured images (median ICC 0.97-0.98). Agreement with experts was maintained across all settings for macro-geometric features (ptosis{rho} = 0.74-0.81, nasolabial fold{rho} = 0.68-0.79) and for discrete pigmentation and inflammatory lesions (pigmented spot density{rho} = 0.62-0.76), declined for fine-texture features under uncontrolled acquisition (forehead wrinkles{rho} = 0.76 to 0.48), and remained limited for color-dependent features irrespective of setting. These findings support the AI-based system as an objective grading tool for a defined subset of facial endpoints in hybrid and DCTs in dermatology.

infographic.key_insight: An AI-based facial grading system matched expert consensus well for larger shape-related and some lesion-based facial features, even when images were captured with less controlled smartphone settings.
infographic.clinical_relevance: This suggests AI-assisted facial assessment could help scale dermatology studies and hybrid/decentralized clinical trials by enabling objective grading outside specialized imaging studios.
method: Compared AI grading with expert panel consensus across standardized studio, clinic smartphone, and home smartphone image settings.
Evaluated repeatability on independently captured images and agreement across feature types.
Assessed performance for geometric, textural, pigmentation, and inflammatory facial endpoints.
infographic.evidence_signal: Experts showed good-to-excellent inter-rater reliability (median ICC 0.84-0.90), and the AI system showed very high test-retest repeatability (median ICC 0.97-0.98) with strongest agreement for macro-geometric features and moderate agreement for pigmented spot density.
infographic.watch_item: Performance dropped for fine-texture and color-dependent features under less controlled acquisition, so these endpoints may be less reliable in home smartphone workflows.
infographic.paper_title: Comparison of Facial Feature Grading by an AI-Based System Versus Human Expert Grading on Images Under Standardized Clinical and At-Home Settings

title: Biomarker Convert: a novel approach to transform plasma pTau217 results across immunoassay and mass spectrometry analytical platforms
authors: Quadrini, K. J.; Aubrecht, J.; Vernhes, F.; Zeng, X.; Johnson, A. D.; Snitz, B. E.; Cohen, A. D.; Tooker, R.; Quiceno, M. E.; Campbell, B. M.; Karikari, T. K.; Swanson, C. J.
abstract: INTRODUCTIONWe report the development and validation of a novel computational tool to cross-convert plasma pTau217 results from different assays to facilitate recruitment for therapeutic trials and observational studies. METHODSParticipants underwent A{beta} PET imaging and plasma pTau217 measurement on up to three assay platforms across three cohorts. We then developed conversion equations using Deming regression - collectively named Biomarker Convert - and evaluated robustness using independent research cohorts. Finally, we modeled the potential impact of pTau217 screening on trial enrollment. RESULTSWhile absolute plasma pTau217 concentrations differed, the assays had similar predictive characteristics for A{beta} positivity (LC-MS/MS [C2N], AUC=0.952; Janssen Simoa, AUC=0.946; Lumipulse, AUC=0.929). Biomarker Convert enabled transformation of plasma pTau217 data across assays independent of A{beta} PET and clinical status. Plasma pTau217 reduced A{beta} PET scans in the model screening paradigm by >60%. DISCUSSIONBiomarker Convert equations enable harmonization of plasma pTau217 values from immunoassay and mass spectrometry platforms, supporting direct data comparison.

infographic.key_insight: Biomarker Convert is a computational harmonization tool that converts plasma pTau217 values across immunoassay and mass spectrometry platforms so results can be compared directly.
infographic.clinical_relevance: By standardizing pTau217 measurements, it could streamline biomarker screening and reduce the number of PET scans needed for trial recruitment and research studies.
method: Built assay-to-assay conversion equations using Deming regression.
Validated the cross-platform transformations in independent research cohorts.
Modeled how pTau217 screening could affect Aβ PET scan use in trial enrollment.
infographic.evidence_signal: Across cohorts, the assays showed similarly strong performance for Aβ positivity detection, with AUCs of 0.929 to 0.952, and the screening model suggested pTau217 could reduce Aβ PET scans by more than 60%.
infographic.watch_item: The conversion equations need careful platform-specific implementation and external validation before widespread use, especially when assays or study populations differ.
infographic.paper_title: Biomarker Convert: a novel approach to transform plasma pTau217 results across immunoassay and mass spectrometry analytical platforms

title: Methylation-associated Gene Expression (MaGE): a non-invasive, in vivo measure of cellular senescence.
authors: Simpson, D. J.; Crofts, S. J.; Mavrommatis, C.; White, T. A.; Suwanlikit, Y. J.; Loyva, K.; Rocca, W. A.; Kantarci, K.; Mielke, M.; Richmond, A.; Marioni, R. E.; Kirschner, K.; LeBrasseur, N. K.; Chandra, T.
abstract: Cellular senescence is a central hallmark of aging, yet its measurement in humans remains invasive, low-throughput and tissue-specific, precluding population-scale study. We developed Methylation-associated Gene Expression (MaGE) predictors: whole-blood DNA methylation proxies of p14ARF, p16INK4A and p21CIP1 expression, plus a composite score, providing the first scalable measure of senescence-marker expression. Deployed across Generation Scotland (n=18,859), MaGE yielded 45 Bonferroni-significant associations spanning 18 incident diseases and all-cause mortality. The two strongest associations recapitulated the established tissue specificity of p21CIP1 and p16INK4A activation, with MaGE-p21 associating with incident alcoholic liver disease and MaGE-p16 with pulmonary fibrosis. In a separate study, MaGE tracked disease severity and treatment response in Crohns disease. MaGE is a scalable, interpretable biomarker of senescence that enables its study at population scale and offers a route to patient stratification in senolytic trials.

infographic.key_insight: MaGE uses blood DNA methylation to non-invasively estimate senescence-marker gene expression, making cellular senescence measurable at population scale.
infographic.clinical_relevance: This could help stratify patients for senolytic trials and support earlier risk tracking for senescence-linked diseases.
method: Built whole-blood methylation proxies for p14ARF, p16INK4A, and p21CIP1 expression, plus a composite score.
Applied the predictors in Generation Scotland (n=18,859) to test links with incident disease and mortality.
Validated utility by tracking disease severity and treatment response in Crohn’s disease.
infographic.evidence_signal: In Generation Scotland, MaGE showed 45 Bonferroni-significant associations across 18 incident diseases and all-cause mortality, with strong tissue-specific signals for p21CIP1 and p16INK4A.
infographic.watch_item: Because the measure is blood-based and tissue-specific biology varies, results may not fully generalize across tissues, diseases, or treatment settings.
infographic.paper_title: Methylation-associated Gene Expression (MaGE): a non-invasive, in vivo measure of cellular senescence.
